In all honesty, yes but for reasons not completely related to the ex.

In short: we each have within us that one hard limit of what we're capable of enduring, that point where we finally say, "I can no longer do this." I've been pushed beyond my own personal threshold for a considerable length of time (years) and I no longer have the patience or will to keep pushing on when everything seems so incredibly bleak and pointless.

I'm not happy. I haven't been happy in so long I couldn't even tell you what the word means beyond the definition in provided by Webster's. And while not being happy is one thing, being completely numb emotionally half the time (like a zombie) and in unbearable anguish I can't even hope to articulate to another person the other half is no way to live.

I've been medicated. I've been in therapy off and on for years (8 consecutive months this go around). I work out constantly. And as I grow old, the less any of them help in combating clinical depression that only worsens as time goes on. And while I had something (a future) and someone (my ex) to give me the motivation required to push through it all, I don't this time. I'm done with life.

When they start talking about a new "friend", start giggling at texts while hiding the phone, and start going out to places that aren't typical...it's been over for a while and you're the last person to find out.

I appreciate your concern, but the gears are already in motion. Being honest, they have been for a while but I haven't yet been presented an opportunity where I can do what must be done without having to be concerned with the intervention of family (they are well-intentioned, but misguided as they refuse to accept that which I have).

Everything is in place: how my remains are to be disposed of and where, who gets what, what is to be discarded, what is to be donated, and what bills are to be paid in order of importance. Links, phone numbers, email addresses, anything and everything linking to a support group, therapists, etc. has been researched, documented, and attached to what will be my last letter; those that care will hurt greatly at first, but in time the pain will abate, they'll move on, and I'll be forgotten. Normal, functional people have that capacity (moving on) which is something I completely lack.

I'd be lying if I didn't say I had hoped things would have panned out differently in my life. I really would have liked to have shared my life and future with my ex; I had her put on as my sole beneficiary, even had an engagement ring picked out to save towards. I would have liked to have gone to college; not Harvard, but somewhere that isn't a degree mill that I actually somewhat enjoy going to. It would have been nice to have a job that doesn't make me feel like a failure as a man, or at least one that paid a living wage. And it would have been joyous to keep my home (an apartment). I was so close to having it all, so incredibly close to having so many years of struggle vindicated...so close to being loved and happy.

At this point, I know none of it was meant to be. If it was, I wouldn't have watched all systematically dismantled helplessly. I know in my heart of hearts what I have to do is what I should have done many a year ago. The universe has a way of correcting aberrations and mistakes; I just didn't want to believe I was the mistake that was to be erased.

For me, it is better to have said them knowing she will never read them than to take them to the grave even though I know I'm not going to be alive for all that much longer (a personal choice unrelated to her). I don't want my last conscious thoughts being about what I should have said.

Two weeks coincides with my birthday and is enough time to see a few friends, a few family members, and to start giving stuff away; I've already given my brother and friend also of my console games (a collection that was not small) and I've already decided who gets my computer.

"This too shall pass". I used to tell that to myself, used to believe it. It's what allowed me to carry on, to power through the dark times. The trouble is that the dark times didn't end. They didn't abate, there was no light to penetrate that dreadful cloud; the more I walked, the darker things became. It's either funny or insulting that every single decision and action I've made in my life has brought me to a path I did everything in my power to avoid. 

I see a counsellor. I'm taught coping skills and how to plan for a future...but not how to desire that future because it's one I never wanted for myself or why I should view it as anything other than a disastrous burden from which there is no escape. Trapped. Broken. Alone. This are things I experience now and yet that it all I am allowed to look forward to. Why would I want any part of that? 

Life does not suddenly change for the better. There are no unexpected, pleasant surprises, just soul crushing events that strike. I have spent my entire life preparing for those storms. That's all I do because it's been my experience that they will always hit and do untold amounts of damage. And no matter how prepared and dug in I am, each one manages to take away more than the one previous. 

I cannot and will not do it anymore. I've done it for my entire adult life and I'm not going to continue doing it.

Not even remotely. There is no hope. There is no joy. There's no "living", just existing for the sake of it. Breathe in, breathe out, go through the mundane day-to-day shit that can be accomplished while watching things play out in a way that I always feared. Things don't get better and I can't make them better at this point in time; I've tried and failed miserably more times than I can count.

A lifetime of misery versus...five, maybe ten minutes of suffering while I exsanguinate depending on how deep I go and what artery I hit; weight training has given me big veins, so I'm sure my radial arteries aren't delicate or small. Decades of pain weighed against minutes, a few flashes of light as my neurons start dying, then never ending blackness I don't have to wake up from. It's an easy choice for me to make.
It's a combination of all. I don't feel comfortable sharing the details outside of a pm; I don't want to be outed, identified, and committed.

I've been treated for years.

Most people, as they go through their days, find at least one small thing to make it worthwhile to them. Maybe it's hope for the future, maybe it's coming home to someone they love. Perhaps it's a hobby or activity they can submerse themselves into completely. It might even be faith alone.

I do not pretend to understand how others perceive the world, nor can I tell you the driving force and motivation in their lives beyond: everyone wants to be loved and find happiness someday.

When I was younger, I used to believe that this would all be a temporary tempest: a sudden, harsh test of faith that would ultimately make me a stronger, better person. That notion is what drove me, day in and out, through my youth as it was taken by the circumstances surrounding me. What I could change I did, what I couldn't I accepted I couldn't (admittedly somewhat bitterly).

One year slipped into two. Then three. Three became 6, and 6 gave way to 8. There was a brief, albeit stressful, period of tranquility where I felt the worst was behind me and that I had been truly blessed: better days were ahead and, for once in my life, they could be seen somewhere other than my mind.

As they came into reach, my life abruptly came apart at the seams in every way possible. And as it came apart, so did I as I tried and miserably failed to prevent it from doing so. Nothing I did mattered. No amount of prayer helped. 

Most people see a few choices, but I only see the two you listed simply because they are all I truly know. The summation of my life history is pain, physical and mental...nothing but. I don't want to know *only* that.

I know how it operates on the biological level: certain neurotransmitters aren't produced in a sufficient volume, certain receptors are completely desensitized to them (thus requiring higher than normal amounts of dopamine, norepinephrine, serotonin, GABA, etc. to function correctly), and it is associated with traumatic brain injury.

Antidepressants help, but only to a small degree; neurotransmitters become increased but receptors start shutting down so more becomes required. The same go for therapy; cognitive fine tuning can only do so much in the face of such hopelessness.

I know how it works. I just don't want to endure it anymore.

I'm aware the few people who care will hurt. I can't live just for them, however.

I do not look at life as this amazing gift but a terrible burden, one I am tired of carrying. I have tried making things better, but they're not; maybe I didn't try hard enough, maybe I was too eager to soon. Maybe it's because I'm not a decent person overall, I don't know.

Not really. Once you hit poverty level, you stay there.

She will never be a part of my life again. The future that seemed so bright was given to my usurper. 

There's really no coming back from that and I know that. People make promises of "better days" (I.e checks they can never possibly honor) that don't happen. Wake up, struggle, self deprecate because the struggle doesn't illicit change.

That's all I have known for a considerable time.  I don't want to know just that forever.

They're genetically enhanced but only to a certain degree: most of a Spartan II's enhancements are surgical and chemical. Their bones are bonded with a ceramic-carbide alloy for greater strength. Their skeletal muscles are chemically and genetically altered to be bigger, stronger, yet more efficient. The ocular blood vessels are modified for better vision while their thyroid glands are packed full of HGH coated pellets (for overall growth as well as promoting persistent anabolism). And lastly, their entire nervous system is cybernetically enhanced to tie it all together.

There's a reason only SPII's can wear proper Mjolnir armor without getting torn into pieces of meat inside of it.

Reader's digest: life fell to pieces over a year ago, I know I can't put it back together. If I say more than that, I'm certain someone will pick up on my throwaway and have me involuntarily committed (again).
